title: InterviewGraph interview records
description: A list of interview records: one job application's interviews, the role it was for, and the questions actually asked. Field reference: docs/data-model.md

question_ids.description: Questions from questions.yaml that were asked in this round, in the order they were asked when known. May be empty for a round nobody recorded.

company.description: The employer's name, or an anonymised label such as 'fintech-a' when company_named is false.

company_named.description: true only when the real company name may be published. Default to false.

industry.description: For example 'fintech', 'media', 'government'. Useful when the company is anonymised.

role_title.description: The title as the posting wrote it.

role_family.description: Normalised role so postings with different titles can be compared.

seniority.description: As the posting framed it, not as you judge it.

date.description: Month of the first round, YYYY-MM. Day-level dates could identify people.

jd_skills.description: Skills and topics the job description asked for, as slugs: 'pytorch', 'rag', 'kubernetes'. This is the public, reusable summary of the JD.

jd_summary.description: Two or three sentences on what the role was really about, in your own words. Never paste the posting.

jd_ref.description: Path to the raw posting on your machine. data/private/ is git-ignored, so the file itself is never published.

source.description: 'self' means the maintainer's own interview; 'community' means a contributor submitted it.

status.description: 'draft' until a person has checked the record and its question links.
